```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Assuming all necessary data has been defined
# expressed_genes: vector of all expressed gene names
# high_CNT: data frame with high count genes
# mitochondrial_genes: vector of mitochondrial gene names
# rrna_genes: vector of rRNA gene names
# protein_coding_genes: vector of protein-coding gene names
# ex_counts: data frame of expression counts with gene names as row names

# Define the genes to keep by excluding unwanted types and retaining protein_coding
keep_genes <- setdiff(
  expressed_genes,
  c(high_CNT$gene_name[1:10], mitochondrial_genes, rrna_genes)
)

# Further filter keep_genes to include only protein_coding genes
keep_genes <- intersect(keep_genes, protein_coding_genes)

# Filter the ex_counts data frame to retain only these genes
cnt.filt <- ex_counts[rownames(ex_counts) %in% keep_genes, ]

# Print or save the filtered data frame
print(cnt.filt)
# write.csv(cnt.filt, 'filtered_ex_counts.csv', row.names = TRUE)
dim(cnt.filt)
```

```{r}
# Step 1: Calculate the mean and standard deviation of the nUmis column
mean_nUmis <- mean(inf$nUMIs, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_nUmis <- sd(inf$nUMIs, na.rm = TRUE)

# Step 2: Define the range of mean ± standard deviation
lower_bound <- mean_nUmis - sd_nUmis
upper_bound <- mean_nUmis + sd_nUmis

# Step 3: Filter the rows within the range
filtered_inf <- inf[inf$nUMIs >= lower_bound & inf$nUMIs <= upper_bound, ]

# Step 4: Extract and display the Sample_ID for these rows
sample_ids_in_range <- filtered_inf$Sample_ID
print(sample_ids_in_range)

```

```{r}
library(DESeq2)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

# Assuming you have a DESeq2 object called `dds`
# Step 1: Transform data using vst or rlog
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = FALSE)  # or use rlog(dds, blind = FALSE)

# Step 2: Perform PCA and extract PC1 and PC2 scores
pca_res <- prcomp(t(assay(vsd)), scale. = TRUE)

# Extract PC1 and PC2 scores
scores <- as.data.frame(pca_res$x[, 1:2])

# Add sample names and group labels
scores$sample <- rownames(scores)
scores$Condition <- colData(vsd)$Condition

# Step 3: Calculate the Euclidean distance from the median for each condition
# Group by condition and calculate the centroids (medians) for PC1 and PC2 within each condition
library(dplyr)

centroids <- scores %>%
  group_by(Condition) %>%
  summarise(PC1_median = median(PC1), PC2_median = median(PC2))

# Merge centroids back to the scores data frame
scores <- merge(scores, centroids, by = "Condition")

# Compute Euclidean distance from the group's centroid for each sample
scores$distance <- apply(scores[, c("PC1", "PC2", "PC1_median", "PC2_median")], 1, function(row) {
  sqrt(sum((row[1:2] - row[3:4])^2))
})

# Step 4: Calculate MAD and identify outliers within each condition
scores <- scores %>%
  group_by(Condition) %>%
  mutate(
    mad_distance = mad(distance),  # Calculate MAD within each group
    mad_threshold = 3 * mad_distance,  # Define outlier threshold as 3 * MAD
    outlier = distance > (median(distance) + mad_threshold)  # Identify outliers within each group
  )

# Print identified outliers
outliers <- scores[scores$outlier == TRUE, ]
print(outliers)

# Step 5: Visualize the PCA plot with outliers highlighted
ggplot(scores, aes(PC1, PC2, color = Condition)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_text_repel(data = scores[scores$outlier == TRUE, ], aes(label = sample), size = 3, color = "red") +
  # Add centroids for each condition
  geom_point(aes(x = PC1_median, y = PC2_median), color = "black", size = 4, shape = 8) +
  geom_text(aes(x = PC1_median, y = PC2_median, label = Condition), vjust = -1, hjust = 0.5, color = "black") +
  xlab(paste0("PC1: ", round(100 * pca_res$sdev[1]^2 / sum(pca_res$sdev^2), 2), "% variance")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2: ", round(100 * pca_res$sdev[2]^2 / sum(pca_res$sdev^2), 2), "% variance")) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal() +
  ggtitle("PCA of RNA-seq Data with Outliers Detected by MAD for Each Condition")

# Step 6: Remove outliers from DESeq2 object (optional)
dds_clean <- dds[, !colnames(dds) %in% outliers$sample]




```

```{r}
varPart <- fitExtractVarPartModel(vsdMat, form, inf)

plotPercentBars(vp[1:10, ])
```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(DESeq2)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Extract normalized counts from the DESeq2 object
normalized_counts <- counts(dds, normalized=TRUE)
##
library(org.Mm.eg.db)
library(GO.db)
library(AnnotationDbi)

# Define the GO term for inflammatory response (GO:0006954)
inflammatory_go_term <- "GO:0006954"

# Get all genes (Entrez IDs) associated with the inflammatory response GO term
inflammatory_genes <- unique(unlist(AnnotationDbi::mget(inflammatory_go_term, org.Mm.egGO2ALLEGS)))

# Map the Entrez gene IDs to gene symbols (mouse genes)
inflammatory_gene_symbols <- unique(unlist(AnnotationDbi::mget(inflammatory_genes, org.Mm.egSYMBOL)))

# Filter the normalized counts for inflammatory genes
genes_of_interest <- rownames(normalized_counts)[rownames(normalized_counts) %in% inflammatory_gene_symbols]

# Output the list of inflammatory genes found in the normalized counts
genes_of_interest

###
# Filter for genes of interest
#genes_of_interest <- grep("^Ccl|^Cxcl|^Mif|^Il|^Ddt|^Stat|^Ifn|^Tlr", rownames(normalized_counts), value = TRUE)
#genes_of_interest <- grep("Stat1|Stat2|Ifnar1", rownames(normalized_counts), value = TRUE)
filtered_counts <- normalized_counts[genes_of_interest, ]

# Convert to a data frame for easier manipulation
df <- as.data.frame(t(filtered_counts))
df$Condition <- colData(dds)$Condition  # Add condition information

# Reshape the data for ggplot2
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Condition, names_to = "gene", values_to = "count")

# Generate the boxplot
ggplot(df_long, aes(x = gene, y = count, fill = Condition)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Normalized Counts of Genes Starting with 'Ccl', 'Cxcl', and 'Mif'",
       x = "Gene",
       y = "Normalized Count")

ggsave("normalized_counts_plot.png", width = 16, height = 6)

# Perform t-tests for each gene
# Perform t-tests for each gene
t_test_results <- df_long %>%
  group_by(gene) %>%
  summarise(p_value = t.test(count ~ Condition)$p.value) %>%
  filter(p_value < 0.05)  # Filter for p-values less than 0.05

# Apply BH correction to the p-values
t_test_results <- t_test_results %>%
  mutate(adjusted_p_value = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")) %>%
  filter(adjusted_p_value < 0.05)  # Filter for adjusted p-values less than 0.05

print(t_test_results)
write.xlsx(t_test_results, "t_test_results.xlsx")

# Generate the boxplot only for significant genes
significant_genes <- t_test_results$gene
df_long_significant <- df_long %>%
  filter(gene %in% significant_genes)

ggplot(df_long_significant, aes(x = gene, y = count, fill = Condition)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Normalized Counts of Significant Genes (p < 0.05)",
       x = "Gene",
       y = "Normalized Count") +
   scale_y_log10()

write.xlsx(df_long_significant, "sig_res.xlsx")

```
